newsitem.title: INDIA: India to sign trade pact with Trinidad and Tobago.
newsitem.headline: India to sign trade pact with Trinidad and Tobago.

text.p: India will sign an agreement with Trinidad and Tobago later this week to boost bilateral trade between the two countries, Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah said on Wednesday.
He told a business seminar on Latin America that the pact, to be signed on Friday, would give exporters and investors in each country better access to the other's markets.

"We are willing to provide all the help that we are capable of to improve bilateral trade with the Latin American countries," said Ramaiah, speaking at a seminar organised by leading Indian industry bodies.
India's trade with Latin American countries rose 160 percent from 12.0 billion rupees in 1990/91 (April-March) to 31.4 billion in 1995/96 (April-March), industry officials said.
The agreement is to be signed in New Delhi during a 14-day official visit by Trinidad's Prime Minister Basdeo Panday.
Panday will be accompanied by his Minister for Foreign Affairs, Ralph Maraj and Minister for Trade and Industry Mervyn Assam as well as a large business delegation.
